author: Mark Atwood
text:
Escalating to human: public-API breaking change to TransportConfig::build_client return type (reqwest::Client → opaque wrapper). Same scope-of-decision family as JMAP-6r7c.50 / .48 / .20 / .26 / .31 — workspace AGENTS.md 'prefer non-breaking; reshape only when bumping a major.'

This finding is the natural extension of JMAP-6lsm.22's SemVer-isolation work: HttpError, WebSocketError, and InvalidHeaderValueError already hide reqwest::Error and tungstenite::Error from the public error surface. TransportConfig::build_client is the remaining seam where reqwest leaks through the public API — it's the contract that says 'this crate uses reqwest forever' for every consumer who has implemented their own TransportConfig.

Bundling recommendation: this is the highest-impact public-API breaking finding in the bd:JMAP-6r7c review epic and is the natural anchor for a coordinated 0.2.0 release of jmap-base-client. Sibling findings to land in the same release:

- JMAP-6r7c.50 (UploadBlobParams reshape)
- JMAP-6r7c.48 (DownloadBlobParams.expected_sha256 → typed Sha256)
- JMAP-6r7c.20 (AuthProvider::auth_header secret-typing)
- JMAP-6r7c.26 (ClientError::Parse / Serialize payload wrapping)
- JMAP-6r7c.31 (WsSession split-half concurrency contract)
- JMAP-6r7c.36 (this bead — TransportConfig return type)

If approved as a 0.2.0 epic, the file an umbrella epic and reassign all six children to it. The downstream propagation cost is meaningful but bounded: jmap-mail-client and jmap-chat-client are the only in-workspace consumers, and neither currently implements its own TransportConfig.

Recommendation: defer until Mark decides whether to open the 0.2.0 epic. None of the six are individually catastrophic; the workspace is pre-1.0 and the current behavior is documented (modulo a few drift findings already fixed in this session).
